//! Dead flag elimination pass.
//!
//! After x86 lifting, arithmetic instructions (ADD, SUB, …) produce separate
//! IR instructions for each RFLAGS bit (CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, OF) but
//! downstream code typically reads only one or two of them (e.g. ZF via a
//! Jcc).  This pass removes flag-producing instructions whose SSA output has
//! zero uses, shrinking the IR before more expensive analyses run.
//!
//! A flag varnode is any `Register`-space varnode in the x86-64 RFLAGS byte
//! range defined in `unlace-lift-x86` (CF..OF at 256..=261).
//!
//! The pass is intentionally narrow: it only removes instructions that
//! produce a flag output.  General dead code is handled by [`DeadCodeElimPass`].
/// Minimum register-space offset for x86 flag bits (CF starts at 256).
const FLAG_OFFSET_MIN: u64 = 256;
const FLAG_OFFSET_END: u64 = 262;
/// Returns `true` if `sv` refers to an x86 RFLAGS bit.
fn is_flag_varnode(sv: &SsaVarnode) -> bool {
    sv.base.space == SpaceId::Register
        && sv.base.offset >= FLAG_OFFSET_MIN
        && sv.base.offset < FLAG_OFFSET_END
}
/// Dead flag elimination: remove instructions whose output is an unused
/// flag varnode.
///

//! Redundant flag-test elimination.
//!
//! x86 (and many other architectures) compute comparisons by issuing a
//! `CMP a, b` (which is `a - b` discarding the result, setting flags) and
//! then testing those flags. The lifter materialises this as
//!
//! ```text
//!     diff = INT_SUB a, b
//!     z    = INT_EQUAL diff, 0
//! ```
//!
//! The `INT_EQUAL ?, 0` pattern is mathematically equivalent to
//! `INT_EQUAL a, b`. The same holds for `INT_NOTEQUAL`. For unsigned
//! less-than, the carry flag of `a - b` is exactly `a < b` — so
//! `INT_LESS(diff_carry_input_a, diff_carry_input_b)` already encodes the
//! comparison. This pass rewrites those pseudo-comparisons through the
//! `INT_SUB` to operate directly on its operands.
//!]

#!/bin/bash
# Golden-diff classifier — audits each failing golden fixture and buckets the
# diff hunks so a human (or agent) can decide refresh-vs-investigate safely.
#
# For every golden under tests/golden/expected/<name>.c it:
#   1. regenerates actual output via `unlace decompile --emit c fixtures/<name>.elf`
#   2. strips the shared IDA prelude (everything before the first `/* Function:`)
#      from BOTH sides so prelude churn (the _OWORD typedef + SSE helper inlines
#      the WIP added) doesn't drown the signal
#   3. diffs the post-prelude bodies and classifies each changed line:
#        PRELUDE   — diff was entirely inside the stripped prelude (safe)
#        SIZE      — only a `Size: 0xNN (NN bytes)` header field changed
#        RENUM     — only a vN/v_N identifier index shifted (cosmetic)
#        STRUCT    — a real structural body change (NEEDS REVIEW)
#   4. prints a per-fixture verdict: REFRESH-SAFE vs NEEDS-REVIEW
#
# Usage: bash scripts/classify_golden_diffs.sh [fixture ...]
#        (no args = all 15 golden fixtures)
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BIN="target/debug/unlace"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "building unlace…" >&2; RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo build -q -p unlace-cli || exit 1; }

fixtures=("$@")

    mapfile -t fixtures < <(ls tests/golden/expected/*.c | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.c$//')
fi

strip_prelude() { awk 'f{print} /^\/\* Function:/{if(!f){f=1; print}}' "$1"; }]

fn assign_names(
    func_name: &str,
    all_vars: &BTreeSet<SsaVarnode>,
    clusters: &[Vec<SsaVarnode>],
) -> BTreeMap<SsaVarnode, String> {
    // Map varnode → cluster index.
    let mut cluster_of: BTreeMap<SsaVarnode, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (i, members) in clusters.iter().enumerate() {
        for sv in members {
            cluster_of.insert(*sv, i);
        }
    }

    // First-appearance order over the canonical sorted varnode iteration.
    // `order` maps cluster index → its final source-level name.
    let mut order: BTreeMap<usize, String> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut next_v_index: u32 = 1;
    let mut next_c_index: u32 = 0;
    for sv in all_vars {
        if let Some(&cidx) = cluster_of.get(sv)
            && let std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(e) = order.entry(cidx)
        {
            let name = if is_coalesced_register_cluster(&clusters[cidx]) {
                let name = format!("c{}", next_c_index);
                next_c_index += 1;
                // A coalesced register cluster still consumes a global ordinal
                // slot, so the `vN` number is skipped rather than reused.
                next_v_index += 1;
                name
            } else {
                let name = format!("v{}", next_v_index);
                next_v_index += 1;
                name
            };
            var_merge_trace_line(&format!(
                "assign-order func={} cluster={} first_sv={:?} name={}",
                func_name, cidx, sv, name
            ));
            e.insert(name);
        }
    }

    // Materialise final names.
    let mut merged: BTreeMap<SsaVarnode, String> = BTreeMap::new();
    for sv in all_vars {
        if let Some(&cidx) = cluster_of.get(sv)
            && let Some(name) = order.get(&cidx)
        {
            merged.insert(*sv, name.clone());
        }
    }
    merged

# Stylistic fixture score against the IDA reference profile.
#
# Runs the golden_fixtures suite with --nocapture, scrapes the
# `[score] <value> <fixture>` lines that Metrics::score() prints to stderr,
# and reports the arithmetic mean across all fixtures. This is a style and
# structural-shape watchdog; it does not measure semantic equivalence or
# DWARF/type-variable accuracy.
#
# Each fixture is also scored once in golden_fixtures_metrics_summary, so
# the stream contains 2 entries per fixture (run + summary). The mean is
# robust to that duplication; both pass through the same scoring formula.
#
# Phase 9 baseline (P9-2 landing): Stylistic Fixture Parity 59.6%
# Per-fixture: medium=0.0 cpp_rtti=50.9 cpp_vtable=53.6 debug_calls=60.0
#              cpp_exceptions=78.2 debug_hello=80.9 debug_structs=93.9
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

cargo_status=0
cargo test -p unlace-test-harness --test golden_fixtures -- --nocapture >"$tmp" 2>&1 \
    || cargo_status=$?

grep -F '[score]' "$tmp" \
    | awk '{ sum += $2; n++ }
           END {
               if (n == 0) {
                   print "no [score] lines found" > "/dev/stderr"
                   exit 1
               }
               printf "Stylistic Fixture Parity: %.1f%%\n", sum / n
           }'

if [ "$cargo_status" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "note: golden_fixtures exited $cargo_status; reported stylistic score from emitted [score] lines" >&2
fi]

# Minimizing Local-Variable Declarations in Decompiler Output

The short answer: production decompilers and the academic literature treat this as **reverse register allocation / out-of-SSA translation**. The decompiler lifts machine code into an SSA-like IR, computes live ranges, builds an interference graph, and then **coalesces** non-interfering SSA values into a single source-level local — the inverse of how a compiler splits one source variable into many machine temporaries. Single-use temporaries are additionally eliminated by **expression propagation** (a guarded copy/value propagation). Soundness rests on the classical **non-interference condition**: two values can share one variable iff their live ranges don't overlap (or they always hold equal values).

A caveat on this answer: the evidence retrieval for this query was poor. Searches for the decompiler-specific literature (Yakdan DREAM/DREAM++, Hex-Rays microcode internals, Lacomis DIRE, Phoenix/TIE) returned **no usable results** [3][5], and the arXiv API failed on both SSA-destruction queries [1][2]. I can only firmly cite the compiler-side SSA/register-allocation and verification literature that did surface [1][2][4]. Claims about Hex-Rays/Ghidra/Binary Ninja internals below are therefore stated from domain knowledge and explicitly flagged as **not supported by the retrieved evidence**.

## (1) Reverse register allocation: SSA-value → source-variable mapping

The core idea is that decompilation runs the compiler back-end transformation in reverse. A compiler does *live-range splitting* and *register allocation*, turning one source variable into many physical-register/stack-slot lifetimes. A decompiler must *merge* those lifetimes back. The standard machinery is:

1. Lift to SSA, giving each definition a fresh value (the `v1, v2, ... v_NN` you see when this step is incomplete).
2. Compute liveness. Efficient SSA liveness via merge sets / DJ-graphs is the relevant primitive here [2 (Das et al., "Efficient liveness computation using merge sets and DJ-graphs", TACO 2012)].
3. Build an **interference graph** over SSA values; two values interfere if their live ranges overlap at some program point.
4. **Coalesce** copy-related and φ-related values that do *not* interfere into a single "web," then assign each web one named local.

The compiler-side analogues that did surface — preference-guided register assignment [1][2 (Braun, Mallon, Hack, "Preference-Guided Register Assignment", CC/LNCS 2010)] and decoupled register allocation via bipartite liveness graphs [2 (Barik, Zhao, Sarkar, TACO 2013)] — are exactly the algorithm shapes a decompiler reuses in reverse: the "preference" to keep copy-related values together is what collapses `v1, v2` into one local.

**Hex-Rays microcode (`mba_t` / `lvar_t` / `udt`), the interference-graph coalescing in Hex-Rays specifically, and any Ghidra/Binary Ninja equivalents are NOT covered by the retrieved evidence** [3][5]. The DBLP/Semantic-Scholar lookups for the decompiler literature returned nothing, so I cannot cite the Hex-Rays lvar-allocation pass or Yakdan's DREAM/DREAM++ from these sources.

## (2) SSA destruction and variable webs

The conceptual frame the question asks for is well established in the compiler literature, though the canonical citations (Cytron et al.; Sreedhar et al.; Boissinot et al., "Revisiting Out-of-SSA Translation for Correctness, Code Quality, and Efficiency") **did not come back in the searches** — the arXiv endpoint failed and OpenAlex/S2 returned only tangential results [1][2].

The standard theory, as reflected in the surfaced register-allocation work [1][2]:

- A **variable** is a connected component of the def-use graph where φ-operands and their results are merged (the **φ-web**), further unioned with copy-related values.
- Two SSA values are **the same variable** when they are φ- or copy-related *and* non-interfering. They are **distinct** when they interfere.
- The **soundness condition** is non-interference: their live ranges must not overlap, **or** they provably always hold equal values (the copy case). Coalescing under this predicate preserves the value seen at every use. This is the precise property the verified-compiler work below proves.

The φ-web definition and out-of-SSA translation (Sreedhar's method, Boissinot's "value-based interference" refinement) are the right references, but I'm flagging that **I could not retrieve them in this run** — treat the attribution as from background knowledge, not from the evidence blocks.

## (3) Folding single-use temporaries (expression propagation)

`v3 = a + b; return v3;` → `return a + b;` is **forward copy/value propagation** with a use-site substitution, and it is the second major source of fewer declared locals (distinct from coalescing in part 1). The dataflow side-conditions that make it sound:

- The temporary has a **single definition** and a **single use** (or all uses are being substituted).
- The def **dominates** the use.
- No **intervening clobber** of any operand (`a`, `b`) between def and use.
- No **intervening side-effect** that the reordering could reorder past (memory writes, volatile loads, calls), preserving the original evaluation order/effects.

When those hold, the temporary's declaration disappears entirely. This is essentially SSA copy propagation restricted to effect-free, single-use defs. **The specific Hex-Rays/Ghidra implementations of this fold are not in the retrieved evidence** — stated from domain knowledge.

## (4) Formalized / verified coalescing and copy-propagation soundness

This is the part the evidence supports most directly. The CompCert line of work formalizes exactly the "coalescing preserves semantics iff no interference" result via **translation validation**:

- **Rideau & Leroy, "Validating Register Allocation and Spilling" (CC 2010, LNCS)** [4]. This is the canonical verified treatment: rather than prove a register allocator correct directly, they *validate its output* — checking a posteriori that the allocation (including coalescing of moves and spill insertion) preserves the source semantics. The validation checker enforces precisely the non-interference / equal-value invariants that coalescing must satisfy; correctness of the checker is mechanically proven. This is the formal backbone for "coalescing is sound iff coalesced values never interfere (or are always equal)." Note this published version appears as LNCS 2010, item 1 in [4] — the same LNCS volume as the Braun/Hack register-assignment paper [1][2], consistent with the CC 2010 proceedings.

- The classical graph-coloring foundation that all coalescing builds on is **Chaitin, "Register Allocation & Spilling via Graph Coloring" (SIGPLAN '82)** [4 (items 3, 5)] and its 2004 reprise [4 (item 2)]. Chaitin's interference graph is the same object decompilers invert; coalescing of move-related nodes that don't interfere is the operation being validated by Rideau & Leroy [4].

The **Blazy/Robert/Leroy** verified-validation extensions you mention are the natural follow-on but **did not appear in the retrieved results**; only Rideau & Leroy [4] is concretely citable here.

## Summary of the algorithm shape

1. Lift → SSA; liveness via merge-sets/DJ-graphs [2].
2. Build interference graph; union φ-webs and copy-related values [1][2].
3. Coalesce non-interfering members of each web → one named local (reverse register allocation; preference-guided to keep copy chains together [1][2]).
4. Propagate single-def/single-use, def-dominates-use, no-clobber/no-side-effect temporaries into their use sites, deleting their declarations.
5. Soundness invariant throughout: coalesced values must be non-interfering or provably equal — exactly the predicate the CompCert validator checks and proves [4].

**Evidence gaps to flag clearly:** the decompiler-specific sources (Hex-Rays microcode/`mba_t`/`lvar_t`/`udt`, Ghidra, Binary Ninja, Yakdan DREAM/DREAM++, Brumley Phoenix/TIE, Schwartz, Lacomis DIRE, "No More Gotos") and the canonical SSA-destruction papers (Cytron, Sreedhar, Boissinot) were **not retrieved** [1][2][3][5]; only the compiler register-allocation [1][2][4] and CompCert validation [4] literature is solidly grounded in the evidence here.

1. **Single def, single use** — exactly one definition and one syntactic use of `v`.
2. **Def dominates use.**
3. **No intervening clobber / no reordering hazard:** `reads(E) ∩ writes(stmts strictly between def and use) = ∅`; and if `E` is impure, no intervening conflicting effect (aliasing write/read, call, volatile).
4. **Single-evaluation preserved** — guaranteed because use-count is exactly 1, so evaluation count is unchanged even for non-idempotent `E`.

This predicate is **local, syntactic, and decidable** on the def-use chains you already have from `compute_live_ranges` + `classify_use_sites`. No interference graph required. //! Compiler-inlined function fold-back (t370).
//!
//! Optimising compilers routinely *inline* short library helpers — `strlen`,
//! `memcpy`, `strcmp`, custom CRC kernels — directly into their callers so
//! the dynamic call overhead disappears. The price is decompiler-output
//! readability: a single `n = strlen(s)` becomes a sprawling loop nest that
//! humans struggle to recognise on sight.
//!
//! This pass scans each SSA block for IR sequences whose *shape* matches a
//! known function's IR fingerprint, and records a "fold-back" suggestion —
//! the block-relative offset where the inline copy starts, plus the inferred
//! function name. Downstream printers can then collapse the matched range
//! and render it as a synthetic call.
//!
//! **MVP scope.** Recognition is purely structural and *detection-only* —
//! no IR is mutated. The fingerprint format is intentionally minimal: a
//! known signature is just an ordered slice of [`IrOp`] discriminants that
//! must appear, in order, somewhere inside a block. Operand-level shape
//! checks (constant zero compares, self-cycle predecessors, etc.) live in
//! the per-function heuristics rather than the generic matcher so the
//! signature table stays declarative.
//!
//! Built-in fingerprints:
//!
//! * `strlen` — `Load, IntEqual, IntAdd, Cbranch` (zero-terminator loop with
//!   a constant-0 compare and a self-cycle back edge).
//! * `memcpy` — `Load, Store, IntAdd, IntAdd, Cbranch` (load/store body with
//!   two pointer-bumps).
//! * `strcmp` — `Load, Load, IntNotequal, IntAdd, Cbranch` (two loads with a
//!   not-equal exit).
//!
//! Callers may pass their own `known_signatures` table to recognise
//! project-specific helpers (e.g. inlined CRC32, RC4 KSA).
/// Result of an inline fold-back scan: one entry per recognised inline copy.
///
/// Each tuple is `(block, body_offset, inferred_name)` where `body_offset`
/// is the index inside the block's instruction list at which the matched
/// fingerprint begins. Multiple matches in the same block are reported
/// independently.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]]

const fn is_never_foldable_op(op: IrOp) -> bool {

            | IrOp::Call
            | IrOp::Callind

            | IrOp::Branchind

            | IrOp::Cpoolref
            | IrOp::Indirect
            | IrOp::Multiequal
    )
}]

(** * CopyPropagation: soundness of single-use temporary folding (NOVEL).

    Measured motivation. unlace decompilation is at type-recovery RECALL 100% but
    PRECISION ~68%: it emits ~200 excess scalar local declarations (`v_NN` /
    `// temp`) that IDA Hex-Rays folds away. The dominant safe lever (confirmed by
    a model council + the Rideau/Leroy and Boissinot out-of-SSA literature) is
    SINGLE-USE EXPRESSION PROPAGATION: when a temporary `t` has one definition
    `t = e` and exactly one use, and the definition dominates the use with no
    intervening clobber, the use can be replaced by `e` and the declaration of
    `t` deleted — strictly fewer locals, identical behaviour.

    This theory mechanizes the soundness predicate the producer's fold must
    satisfy. We model a straight-line statement sequence over a variable store
    and prove:

      1. SUBSTITUTION SOUNDNESS — folding `t := e; … ; u := f[t]` into
         `…(t removed)…; u := f[e]` yields the SAME final store for `u`, provided
         no statement strictly between the def and the use writes any variable
         read by `e` (the no-clobber / no-intervening-write condition), and `t`
         is not read anywhere else (single use).

      2. DECLARATION ELISION — after folding, `t` is dead (no remaining read), so
         dropping its assignment preserves the whole store on the live
         variables. This is the part that actually lowers the local-declaration
         count (folding without elision gains nothing).

      3. NON-INTERFERENCE FRAMING — the clobber-freedom hypothesis is exactly the
         decompiler-side specialization of the register-allocation
         non-interference predicate (Rideau-Leroy): the folded value's operands
         keep their def-time values at the use site.

# ws-deque

A lock-free, **dependency-free**, **ThreadSanitizer-clean** Chase-Lev work-stealing deque in
safe-surface Rust — the scheduling primitive that underlies Rayon, Tokio, and Go, implemented
from the original papers for study and standalone use.

```rust
use ws_deque::{Worker, Steal};

let worker = Worker::new();          // single owner: push/pop at the bottom
let stealer = worker.stealer();      // any number of thieves: steal from the top

worker.push(1);
worker.push(2);
assert_eq!(worker.pop(), Some(2));   // owner pops LIFO
assert!(matches!(stealer.steal(), Steal::Success(1))); // thieves take FIFO
```

Or use the built-in **lifeline-graph scheduler** for irregular fork-join workloads — idle
workers park spin-free and are woken via a hypercube lifeline graph, with clean distributed
termination:

```rust
use ws_deque::scheduler::run;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

let count = AtomicUsize::new(0);
run(8, [20u32], |depth, spawner| {        // 8 workers, one seed task
    count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    if depth > 0 {
        spawner.spawn(depth - 1);          // each task may spawn more
        spawner.spawn(depth - 1);
    }
});
// runs the whole dynamically-unfolding tree to completion, then returns
```

Need **priority** (expand promising work first)? `priority::PriorityWorker<T, K>` layers `K`
priority levels over the deque — `pop`/`steal` always take the highest-priority task. On A\* vs
Dijkstra it explores ~5× fewer nodes for the same optimum (the Wimmer "priority reduces total
